papers.title: A transcriptomics-based computational drug repurposing pipeline identifies simvastatin and primaquine as therapeutics for endometriosis.
papers.abstract: Endometriosis has limited treatment options, prompting the search for data-driven therapeutics. We previously used a transcriptomics-based computational drug repositioning pipeline and identified several drug candidates. Fenoprofen, our top in silico candidate, was validated in a rat model of endometriosis-associated pain. Building on this, we evaluated two additional candidates, simvastatin and primaquine. Using the rat model, we conducted behavioral testing, bulk RNA sequencing, and differential expression analysis to assess their therapeutic potential. We also assessed endometriosis diagnos
papers.summary: This study applies a transcriptomics-based computational drug repurposing pipeline to identify simvastatin and primaquine as potential endometriosis therapeutics, building on prior work that validated fenoprofen. Using a rat model, the authors performed behavioral testing and bulk RNA sequencing to assess therapeutic effects. The findings support these candidates as promising repurposed drugs for endometriosis, though the abstract is truncated.

papers.title: Global Research Trends and Insights on AI Usage in Tuberculosis: Bibliometric Analysis.
papers.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) remains a major global health challenge despite prevention efforts. AI offers promising approaches to long-standing challenges in TB diagnosis, drug resistance detection, and case management; however, a systematic mapping of global research priorities and translational gaps in AI applications to TB is currently lacking.
papers.summary: This bibliometric analysis maps global research trends and priorities in the application of AI to tuberculosis, covering areas such as diagnosis, drug resistance detection, and case management. It identifies key research hotspots and translational gaps, providing a systematic overview of where the field is heading and where clinical translation lags.

papers.title: From QSAR to deep learning: an interpretable comprehensive pipeline with a read-across approach for mutagenicity prediction via the Enalos Cloud Platform.
papers.abstract: Assessing the mutagenicity of chemical compounds is essential for ensuring their safe handling and use, thereby minimizing potential health risks. New approach methodologies (NAMs), including computational approaches, provide non-animal alternatives for testing novel materials and chemicals. This study highlights the potential of in silico NAMs, which can contribute to the development of novel Safe and Sustainable by Design (SSbD) chemicals and substances by identifying potentially hazardous ones at an early stage. Emphasis is given to the mutagenicity prediction based on data from the Ames (b
papers.summary: This paper presents an interpretable computational pipeline that combines QSAR modeling, deep learning, and a read-across approach to predict chemical mutagenicity using Ames test data. The tool is deployed on the Enalos Cloud Platform, offering a non-animal alternative for early-stage hazard screening of chemicals. It supports Safe and Sustainable by Design (SSbD) efforts by flagging potentially mutagenic compounds before synthesis or use.

papers.title: Decision-grade evidence for AI-enabled small-molecule discovery.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence now guides choices across small-molecule discovery, yet benchmark gains rarely reveal whether a model changed the next compound, assay or project decision. This Perspective organizes public evidence around Design, Make, Test and Analyze (DMTA) handoffs. It distinguishes reproducible benchmark evidence (C1), use-relevant retrospective robustness (C2), executed Make or Test handoffs (C3), prospective workflow comparisons (C4-W) and traceable downstream trajectories (C4-D), with separate Evaluation, Deliverability and Governance profiles. Two authors independently screened
papers.journal: SLAS discovery : advancing life sciences R & D
papers.summary: This Perspective proposes a framework for evaluating AI in small-molecule discovery by organizing evidence around Design-Make-Test-Analyze (DMTA) handoffs rather than benchmark performance alone. It defines five evidence tiers (C1-C4) distinguishing reproducible benchmarks, retrospective robustness, executed handoffs, prospective workflow comparisons, and traceable downstream outcomes, with separate profiles for evaluation, deliverability, and governance. The goal is to help researchers and decision-makers assess whether AI models actually influence real compound, assay, or project decisions.

papers.title: Integrated experimental and computational evaluation of atractylenolide III from Tubipora musica for anticancer lead identification.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a major global health challenge, with over 900,000 new cases annually and a pronounced male predominance. In pursuit of novel, low-toxicity therapeutics, this study isolated Atractylenolide III from the marine coral Tubipora musica and demonstrated measurable, dose-dependent cytotoxic activity against HepG2 liver cancer cells, achieving an IC50 value of 15.50 µg/mL and reducing cell viability to 25.0% at 25 µg/mL. To investigate potential molecular targets and propose hypothetical mechanism pathways, we employed a multi-layered computational strategy. Mol
papers.summary: This study isolated Atractylenolide III from the marine coral Tubipora musica and showed it kills HepG2 liver cancer cells in a dose-dependent manner (IC50 = 15.50 µg/mL). Computational docking and network analyses were then used to propose hypothetical molecular targets and mechanisms underlying its anticancer activity.

papers.title: Cross-docking and redocking reveal distinct determinants of success in physics-based and AI-driven binding pose prediction in protein-ligand complexes.
papers.abstract: Protein-ligand pose prediction is central to structure-based drug discovery, yet the relative performance of physics-based and AI-driven methods under realistic cross-docking conditions remains insufficiently characterized. Here, we compare physics-based docking methods (AutoDock4, AutoDock Vina, and DOCK 6) with data-driven approaches, including the deep-learning model GNINA 1.3 and the diffusion-based frameworks AlphaFold 3, Boltz-2, and DiffDock. Performance was evaluated using standardised redocking and cross-docking protocols across three Alzheimer's disease targets representing distinct
papers.summary: This study benchmarks physics-based docking tools (AutoDock4, AutoDock Vina, DOCK 6) against AI-driven pose predictors (GNINA 1.3, AlphaFold 3, Boltz-2, DiffDock) under both redocking and cross-docking conditions on three Alzheimer's disease targets. The authors find that the two method classes have distinct determinants of success, with AI methods excelling in some regimes while physics-based methods remain competitive in others. The work highlights that realistic cross-docking evaluation is essential for fairly assessing binding pose prediction performance.

papers.title: Revisiting the LSER Approach in the Era of Machine Learning: Insights from IAM Chromatography.
papers.abstract: The present study demonstrates the integration of the linear solvation energy relationship (LSER) concept with machine learning (ML) methodologies to improve the predictive and interpretative capabilities of chromatographic retention modeling. Immobilized artificial membrane (IAM) chromatography was employed as a model biochromatographic system, and an in-house library of 993 structurally diverse compounds, with experimentally determined chromatographic hydrophobicity index of IAM (CHIIAM), was used to train LSER-ML models. LSER descriptors were calculated using Absolv and extended with ioniza
papers.summary: This study combines the classical linear solvation energy relationship (LSER) framework with machine learning to model chromatographic retention on immobilized artificial membrane (IAM) columns. Using a library of 993 diverse compounds with measured CHIIAM values, the authors show that LSER descriptors augmented with ionization features can improve both prediction and interpretation of retention behavior. The work demonstrates how traditional physicochemical modeling concepts can be enhanced by ML in the era of data-driven chemistry.

papers.title: A deep learning framework for oligopeptide candidate discovery across metabolism-related contexts.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-based methods are increasingly critical in therapeutic peptide discovery but have been concentrated in certain applications, such as the development of antimicrobial peptides. Therapeutic peptide discovery in contexts such as metabolism, endocrinology, and tissue regeneration remains challenging due to a paucity of available indication-specific training data. Here, we propose a deep learning-based pipeline, Deepeptide, capable of identifying candidate oligopeptides for various metabolism-related contexts. Leveraging the intrinsic relationships between disease indic
papers.summary: The authors present Deepeptide, a deep learning pipeline designed to discover therapeutic oligopeptides for metabolism-related conditions such as metabolic disorders, endocrinology, and tissue regeneration, areas where training data are scarce. By leveraging relationships between disease indications and peptide properties, the framework identifies candidate peptides without requiring large indication-specific datasets. This expands AI-driven peptide discovery beyond well-studied areas like antimicrobial peptides.

papers.title: Bioactive compounds from marine algae targeting MMP-9: A computational approach to rheumatoid arthritis treatment.
papers.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune systemic inflammatory condition that significantly damages bone and cartilage, leading to severe joint deformities. Matrix metalloproteinase(s) (MMP-9) plays a significant role in both the pathogenesis and management of RA, and its status as a biomarker and a target for inhibition is important in understanding and treating the disease. This work aims to examine the interactions between the molecules of MMP-9 and bioactive compounds derived from marine algae using molecular docking and absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicit
papers.summary: This study uses molecular docking and ADMET predictions to screen bioactive compounds from marine algae as potential inhibitors of MMP-9, a matrix metalloproteinase implicated in rheumatoid arthritis pathogenesis and joint destruction. The computational approach identifies candidate compounds with favorable binding interactions and drug-like properties, suggesting marine algae as a source of anti-RA therapeutics. Findings are preliminary and require experimental validation.

papers.title: From chemical space to synthetic reality: A framework for makeable-by-design generative AI in drug discovery.
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping molecular design, but many outputs are still judged by proxy metrics that do not establish whether proposed compounds can be synthesized, tested and advanced. This review reframes the field around 'synthetic reality': the extent to which AI-generated molecules survive route planning, precursor availability, experimental execution and medicinal chemistry decision-making. We examine the limits of heuristic synthesizability metrics, assess route-aware and execution-facing systems and propose maturity levels, reporting standards, actionability m
papers.summary: This review argues that generative AI in drug discovery should be evaluated not by proxy metrics like synthesizability scores but by 'synthetic reality'—whether proposed molecules can actually be made, tested, and advanced through real medicinal chemistry workflows. It critiques current heuristic metrics, surveys route-aware and execution-facing systems, and proposes maturity levels and reporting standards to make AI-generated molecules 'makeable by design'.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence and ultra-high performance computing methods and experiments for drug discovery: virtual screening, deep learning, molecular dynamics simulations, ADMET modelling, and experimental validation.
papers.abstract: Recent years have witnessed considerable progress in computer-aided drug discovery, driven by the incorporation of computational technologies within both academic and pharmaceutical environments. This evolution is marked by a significant accumulation of data pertaining to detailed three-dimensional structural information, ligand properties, and their interactions with therapeutic targets. The augmentation of computational capabilities and the accessibility of extensive chemical libraries containing billions of drug-like small molecules have further facilitated this transition. To effectively u
papers.summary: This review surveys the integration of AI and ultra-high-performance computing across the drug discovery pipeline, covering virtual screening, deep learning, molecular dynamics simulations, ADMET modelling, and experimental validation. It highlights how massive chemical libraries and growing structural data are enabling more efficient computational drug discovery workflows.

papers.title: Stable simulations do not guarantee functional engagement: a case study of off-target prediction for Seladelpar and Zanamivir.
papers.abstract: Identifying off-target interactions of approved drugs is important to anticipate side effects and uncover repurposing opportunities. Computational pipelines combining structural homology, structure prediction, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations offer a promising strategy, but it remains unclear whether stable, control-like MD trajectories reliably indicate functional engagement. We examined this in a case study of two approved drugs. Using the Evolutionary Classification of Protein Domains (ECOD) framework to select candidate off-targets, we modeled each drug-protein complex as two indepe
papers.summary: This study tests whether stable molecular dynamics simulations of drug-protein complexes reliably predict true off-target binding, using Seladelpar and Zanamivir as case studies. The authors find that stable, control-like trajectories do not guarantee functional engagement, cautioning against over-reliance on MD stability as evidence for off-target interactions.

papers.title: From diligence to verification: the emergence of the TechBio-Investor.
papers.abstract: Recent technical advances, including AI co-scientists and agentic systems, increasingly allow TechBios to undertake scientific verification at scale. In addition to facilitating internal discovery efforts, these capabilities can also be used for making external investment decisions. The emerging synergies between discovery and investment enable a new type of hybrid entity, the TechBio-Investor, which has the potential to reshape the economics and ethics of biotech investing. Scaled verification can help improve capital allocation, steering investment toward stronger science and, in a sector wh
papers.summary: This perspective article argues that AI-driven tools such as co-scientists and agentic systems now let TechBio companies perform scientific verification at scale, not just for internal discovery but also for evaluating external investments. This convergence creates a new hybrid entity, the 'TechBio-Investor,' which could reshape the economics and ethics of biotech investing by steering capital toward stronger science.

papers.title: Task-adaptive multimodal molecular representations for structure-sensitive property prediction.
papers.abstract: Structure-sensitive properties (SSPs), including activity cliffs and chirality-dependent properties, challenge molecular machine learning because small structural perturbations can cause abrupt property changes and invalidate smooth structure-property assumptions. Here, we present CAMF (Chirality- and Activity-cliff-aware Multimodal Framework), a task-adaptive framework that models SSPs through selective integration of complementary molecular evidence. To systematically evaluate this problem, we construct SSPBench, a benchmark spanning 77 conventional ADMET and physicochemical tasks together w
papers.summary: The paper introduces CAMF, a task-adaptive multimodal framework for predicting structure-sensitive molecular properties such as activity cliffs and chirality-dependent effects, where small structural changes cause large property shifts. It also presents SSPBench, a benchmark of 77 ADMET and physicochemical tasks designed to systematically evaluate these challenging prediction scenarios. The approach selectively integrates complementary molecular representations to improve performance on tasks that violate smooth structure-property assumptions.

papers.title: New thinking for the next generation of antimalarials.
papers.abstract: Despite decades of intensive research and substantial clinical gains, malaria remains a major global health challenge exacerbated by the continued emergence of drug-resistant strains of the causative agent, Plasmodium parasites. Encouragingly, recent advances in functional genomics, chemical biology and computational science are reshaping antimalarial drug discovery. In this review, we examine the discovery and development of next-generation antimalarials, including advances in phenotypic and target-based screening, omics-enabled target discovery and emerging therapeutic modalities such as lon
papers.summary: This review discusses how recent advances in functional genomics, chemical biology, and computational science are transforming the discovery of next-generation antimalarial drugs. It covers phenotypic and target-based screening, omics-driven target identification, and emerging therapeutic modalities, all aimed at combating drug-resistant Plasmodium parasites.

papers.title: Expanding Quantitative Medicines' Reach: Systems and Methods to Enhance R&D Productivity and Decision-Making in the Agentic-Era.
papers.abstract: Despite integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into drug discovery and an expanding global medicines pipeline, new drug approvals have declined, highlighting a paradox in biopharma: More drugs discovered, but less approvals, higher costs, and longer timelines. Reasons for the decreased research and development (R&D) efficiency are multifactorial, in part driven by the complexity of new modalities, difficult targets and indications, and persistence of cognitive biases in clinical decision-making. One proposed solution to address R&D productivity challenges includes the adoption of organiza
papers.summary: This paper examines the paradox in biopharma R&D where AI-driven drug discovery has expanded the pipeline yet new drug approvals have declined, with rising costs and longer timelines. The authors propose that adopting quantitative medicines approaches—including systems and methods to enhance decision-making in the emerging 'agentic era' of AI—could improve R&D productivity. The work is largely a perspective on organizational and methodological strategies rather than a primary research study.

papers.title: Decoupling topological and molecular features for interpretable biomolecular interaction prediction.
papers.abstract: Predicting biomolecular interactions is fundamental to understanding cellular mechanisms and advancing drug discovery. However, biomolecular interactions exhibit immense diversity across multiple dimensions. Most existing computational methods are designed to handle one specific task or data modality, which limits their applicability and generalization capability in broader scenarios. To address this methodological rigidity, we propose a flexible framework for multi-modal feature fusion in biomolecular interaction prediction (FlexBIP). The core of FlexBIP lies in its modular architecture, whic
papers.summary: FlexBIP is a modular framework for predicting biomolecular interactions that decouples topological and molecular features, allowing flexible fusion of multi-modal data. It aims to overcome the rigidity of existing task- or modality-specific methods, improving generalization across diverse interaction prediction scenarios. The approach emphasizes interpretability by separating structural (topological) from sequence/chemical (molecular) information.

papers.title: Comprehensive evaluation of AlphaFold/OpenFold prediction of experimentally unresolved proteins through novel metrics.
papers.abstract: Predicting accurate protein structures is essential for understanding molecular mechanisms, interpreting the impact of sequence variation, and supporting translational applications ranging from drug discovery to clinical genomics. Recent advances in deep-learning-based predictors such as AlphaFold2, OpenFold, and AlphaFold3 have transformed structural biology, enabling routine in silico modeling even for challenging or previously uncharacterized proteins. However, systematic benchmarking of these tools-especially for novel targets and single amino acid variants-remains limited. Conventional gl
papers.summary: This paper systematically benchmarks AlphaFold2, OpenFold, and AlphaFold3 on experimentally unresolved proteins and single amino acid variants using novel evaluation metrics. It addresses a gap in understanding how these deep-learning structure predictors perform on novel targets where no experimental ground truth exists. The work provides guidance for interpreting predicted structures in translational and clinical genomics contexts.

papers.title: Ethical Considerations on Artificial Intelligence, Health and Health Care. All That Glisters Is Not Gold.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming global health care through innovations in deep learning, generative models and agentic AI systems. Traditional reductionist approaches to complex pathophysiological pathways fail to capture the true complexity of disease, motivating the adoption of network medicine (NM), which models biological systems as dynamic, interconnected networks. When combined with AI, NM enables integration of multiomic data and better characterizes disease mechanisms to guide precision therapies. Nevertheless, the rapid diffusion of AI in health care also raises profound
papers.summary: This paper discusses how artificial intelligence, combined with network medicine, is transforming healthcare by modeling diseases as interconnected biological networks and integrating multiomic data for precision therapies. However, it emphasizes that the rapid adoption of AI in healthcare raises profound ethical concerns that must be carefully addressed. The authors caution that not all that appears promising in AI-driven healthcare is genuinely beneficial.

papers.title: Discovery of novel acridine based inhibitors of Bruton's tyrosine kinase (BTK) via pharmacophore modeling and machine learning-driven virtual screening followed by molecular dynamic studies.
papers.abstract: Bruton's Tyrosine Kinase (BTK) has been recently recognized as an important drug design target for treating B-cell malignancies. Unfortunately, drug resistance is making the treatment of B-cell malignancies challenging. In this study, we employed a dual machine learning drug design approach that involves two parallel branches: the QSAR-GFA modeling (Branch 1) which engages the development of an interpretable structure activity relationships, and the KNIME® based machine learning modeling (Branch 2) which aimed at achieving high predictive accuracy. Subsequently, six machine learning modules, e
papers.summary: This study identifies new acridine-based inhibitors of Bruton's Tyrosine Kinase (BTK), a key target in B-cell malignancies where drug resistance is a growing problem. The authors combined pharmacophore modeling with a dual machine learning approach—interpretable QSAR-GFA modeling and KNIME-based predictive modeling—to virtually screen compounds, then validated top candidates through molecular dynamics simulations. The work demonstrates how integrating interpretable and high-accuracy ML models can streamline hit discovery against resistance-prone kinase targets.

papers.title: Correction to: Structure-informed machine learning for drug discovery: a task-centric perspective.
papers.summary: This is a correction notice for a previously published review article on structure-informed machine learning for drug discovery from a task-centric perspective. It does not present new research findings, but rather amends or clarifies aspects of the original publication. The correction ensures the accuracy and integrity of the review's content.

papers.title: Novel indole alkaloids from the flower buds of Panax vietnamensis var. fuscidiscus: Distribution in reproductive organs and integrated biological evaluation.
papers.abstract: While the chemical constituents of flower buds from several Panax species have been reported, the phytochemical profile of the flower buds of Vietnamese ginseng remains understudied, particularly alkaloids. This study aimed to characterize alkaloids from the flower buds of Panax vietnamensis var. fuscidiscus (PVF), investigate their distribution across reproductive plant parts, and their biological relevance.
papers.summary: This study characterizes novel indole alkaloids from the flower buds of Panax vietnamensis var. fuscidiscus, a previously understudied Vietnamese ginseng variety. The authors map the distribution of these alkaloids across reproductive organs and evaluate their biological activities, expanding the known phytochemical profile of Panax species.

papers.title: GC-MS-Based Phytochemical Profiling and Integrated Evaluation of Antioxidant, Antibacterial, and In Silico Studies of Kumaun Himalayan Strobilanthes Species.
papers.abstract: Five Strobilanthes species indigenous to the Kumaun Himalayan region of Uttarakhand, India, have been historically employed in traditional medicine to treat bacterial infections, inflammatory conditions, and respiratory ailments, but remain largely unexplored for aquaculture disease management applications. Dichloromethane extracts of S. glutinosa (SGDE), S. pentastemonoides (SPDE), S. angustifrons (SADE), S. attenuata (SATDE) and S. tomentosa (STDE) were comprehensively analysed by GC-MS for phytochemical profiling, with antioxidant activity quantified using DPPH radical scavenging and ferroz
papers.summary: This study profiled the phytochemical composition of dichloromethane extracts from five Strobilanthes species native to the Kumaun Himalaya using GC-MS, and evaluated their antioxidant and antibacterial activities alongside in silico docking analyses. The work highlights these traditionally used medicinal plants as potential sources of bioactive compounds, with possible applications in aquaculture disease management.

papers.title: Synthesis, X-ray structures and biological evaluation of novel α-aminophosphonate derivatives as anti-inflammatory and antioxidant agents: an integrated in vitro and in silico study.
papers.abstract: In the field of medicinal chemistry, the design of small molecules is acknowledged as an effective strategy. This study may contribute to the global fight against inflammatory diseases by focusing on the synthesis of novel α-aminophosphonate derivatives incorporating para-aminobenzoic acid (PABA) and benzocaine moieties and evaluating their anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities. Compounds 1a-1i, 2a-2g and 3a-3f were efficiently prepared via a one-pot Kabachnik-Fields reaction in moderate to high yields. Structural characterization was achieved using spectroscopic techniques and single-c
papers.summary: This study synthesized a series of novel α-aminophosphonate derivatives incorporating PABA and benzocaine scaffolds via a one-pot Kabachnik-Fields reaction, then characterized them using spectroscopy and X-ray crystallography. The compounds were evaluated for anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activity using both in vitro assays and in silico docking, identifying promising lead candidates for further medicinal chemistry development.

papers.title: Phytochemical Profiling and Antibacterial Activity of Moroccan Monofloral Honeys Against Multidrug-Resistant Uropathogens: In Vitro, ADMET, Molecular Docking, and Molecular Dynamics Approaches.
papers.abstract: Urinary tract infections represent a significant public health issue exacerbated by bacterial antibiotic resistance. Honey, due to its phenolic compounds, offers a promising natural alternative. This study explores the phenolic profile of monofloral honeys from the Beni Mellal-Khenifra region and their antibacterial activity against multidrug-resistant strains. Four monofloral honeys from Beni Mellal-Khenifra were analyzed for their phenolic composition and evaluated for antibacterial activity against multidrug-resistant uropathogenic bacteria. Computational studies were also performed to expl
papers.summary: This study characterizes the phenolic compounds in four Moroccan monofloral honeys and tests their antibacterial activity against multidrug-resistant urinary tract pathogens. It combines in vitro assays with computational ADMET, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics to explore how honey phytochemicals may inhibit bacterial targets. The work supports honey as a potential natural source of antibacterial compounds, though findings remain preliminary and specific to these regional samples.

papers.title: Decoding cancer with artificial intelligence: Transforming research, diagnosis, and therapy with future insights.
papers.abstract: Cancer remains one of the leading global health burdens, with increasing complexity in genomic, imaging, and clinical datasets presenting significant challenges for effective management. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a powerful tool to address these challenges by enabling pattern recognition, knowledge integration, and data-driven decision-making. This review highlights recent advances in the application of AI across cancer research, diagnosis, and therapy. In research, AI accelerates drug discovery and repurposing, enhances genomic data interpretation, and facilitates biomarker
papers.summary: This review surveys recent advances in applying artificial intelligence across cancer research, diagnosis, and therapy, covering drug discovery and repurposing, genomic data interpretation, and biomarker identification. It argues that AI can help manage the growing complexity of genomic, imaging, and clinical datasets in oncology.

papers.title: A cross-species drug-discovery platform to accelerate the identification of lifespan-extending interventions.
papers.abstract: We develop an integrated, high-throughput platform to evaluate pharmacological lifespan-extending interventions across five model organisms spanning unicellular to mammalian biology including yeast, nematodes, fruit flies, killifish, and mice. By combining automated imaging, miniaturized assays, and deep-learning-based death detection, we evaluate over 400 compounds across thousands of conditions. In S. cerevisiae, a miniaturized PI/flow cytometry CLS assay enables scalable screening and identifies key assay confounders, while in C. elegans and D. melanogaster, compact imaging platforms couple
papers.summary: The authors built a cross-species drug-discovery platform that tests compounds for lifespan extension across yeast, nematodes, fruit flies, killifish, and mice, using automated imaging and deep-learning-based death detection. Screening over 400 compounds across thousands of conditions, they identify candidate lifespan-extending interventions and highlight assay confounders in yeast chronological lifespan assays. The work provides a scalable, comparative framework for aging drug discovery.

papers.title: Olfactory proteomics reveals the capacity of the HDAC1 inhibitor pyroxamide to halt the α-synuclein preformed fibrils-induced damage in nasal epithelial, microglial and dopaminergic neuronal cell lines.
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is the second most common neurodegenerative disorder mainly characterized by the degeneration of dopaminergic neurons originating in the substantia nigra (SN) pars compacta and projecting to other brain regions, giving rise to motor and non-motor symptoms. Despite significant progress in understanding the molecular and cellular disruptions associated with PD, there remains an unmet clinical need for effective therapies. In this study, proteomic analysis of the olfactory tract (OT) in controls with no known neurological history (n = 17) and PD subjects (n = 21) revealed
papers.summary: This study uses proteomic analysis of the olfactory tract to compare Parkinson's disease patients with controls, identifying molecular changes associated with the disease. The authors then show that the HDAC1 inhibitor pyroxamide can protect nasal epithelial, microglial, and dopaminergic neuronal cell lines from damage induced by α-synuclein preformed fibrils, suggesting a potential therapeutic avenue.

papers.title: Predicting Single-Cell Perturbation Responses Across Biological Contexts With a Deep Generative Model Integrating Optimal Transport.
papers.abstract: Predicting how single cells respond to perturbations is a central problem in computational biology, with potential relevance to emerging artificial intelligence virtual cell (AIVC) research and drug-discovery efforts. However, substantial variation in perturbation responses across biological contexts and the limited generalizability of current models make prediction across cell types, patients, species, and other contexts particularly challenging. To address this challenge, we present single-cell perturbation inference via latent optimal transport (scPILOT), a query-conditioned framework for t
papers.summary: The authors present scPILOT, a deep generative model that integrates optimal transport to predict single-cell perturbation responses across diverse biological contexts such as cell types, patients, and species. The query-conditioned framework aims to overcome the limited generalizability of existing models, supporting applications in virtual cell research and drug discovery.

papers.title: Molecular insights and ADMET profiling of iridoids as candidate leads for erectile dysfunction therapy.
papers.abstract: Erectile dysfunction (ED) significantly affects male psychosocial health and has an increasing incidence. Although phosphodiesterase 5 (PDEi-5) inhibitors are the first-line therapy, the occurrence of visual side effects resulting from cross-inhibition of the PDE-6 isoform limits their adoption. In this context, the plant Veronica anagallis-aquatica L. emerges as a promising source of bioactive therapeutic compounds. This work investigated the inhibitory potential and selectivity of eight iridoid glycosides from this species against PDE-5 and PDE-6. The results identified catalposide as the mo
papers.summary: This study uses molecular modeling and ADMET profiling to evaluate eight iridoid glycosides from Veronica anagallis-aquatica as potential PDE-5 inhibitors for erectile dysfunction, aiming to avoid the visual side effects caused by PDE-6 cross-inhibition. Catalposide was identified as the most promising lead compound based on its inhibitory potential and selectivity.

papers.title: Bridging the AI Divide in Drug Discovery: Practical Lessons from Capacity Strengthening in Africa.
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become an integral part of drug discovery in high-income countries. However, these advances have yet to be broadly adopted by research ecosystems in many low- and middle-income countries in Africa, where understudied infectious diseases, compounded by a growing noncommunicable disease burden, cause millions of deaths each year. Given adequate support and appropriate models AI could play a transformative role in under-resourced biomedical research ecosystems in Africa, democratizing drug discovery research. There is an urgent need to invest in building the criti
papers.summary: This perspective article examines the gap in AI adoption for drug discovery between high-income countries and African research ecosystems, where infectious and noncommunicable disease burdens remain high. The authors argue that with adequate support and context-appropriate models, AI could democratize drug discovery in under-resourced settings, and they call for investment in capacity strengthening across the continent.

papers.title: Accelerate Your Science: Direct-to-Biology Strategies in Medicinal Chemistry.
papers.abstract: Direct-to-biology (D2B) is a powerful strategy that accelerates early drug discovery. It enables compounds to be synthesized in miniaturized formats and evaluated directly as crude reaction mixtures. This bypasses the need for purification during the initial design-make-test cycle. Advances in robust synthetic methodologies, automation, reaction miniaturization, and biological screening have transformed D2B from a proof-of-concept approach into a versatile medicinal chemistry platform. This platform is applicable to fragment optimization, covalent ligands, macrocycles, proteolysis-targeting ch
papers.summary: This review describes direct-to-biology (D2B) strategies, where compounds are synthesized in miniaturized formats and screened directly as crude reaction mixtures, skipping purification in the early design-make-test cycle. Advances in robust synthesis, automation, miniaturization, and biological screening have turned D2B from a proof-of-concept into a versatile platform for fragment optimization, covalent ligands, macrocycles, and PROTACs.

papers.title: Evaluating the outputs of ARAE-based molecular generative model for synthetic accessibility and BTK inhibition.
papers.abstract: The application of artificial intelligence (AI) methodologies in drug discovery represents a rapidly expanding area of interest, providing a valuable means for exploring uncharted chemical spaces to identify novel therapeutic candidates. In this proof-of-concept study, we evaluated hypothetical drug-like molecules generated by an adversarial regularized autoencoder (ARAE) architecture, which were not documented in existing chemical literature and databases, for their synthetic tractability and inhibitory effects on Bruton's tyrosine kinase (BTK). Utilizing a structure-based computational appro
papers.summary: This proof-of-concept study evaluates novel drug-like molecules generated by an adversarial regularized autoencoder (ARAE) for their synthetic accessibility and ability to inhibit Bruton's tyrosine kinase (BTK). The authors use structure-based computational methods to assess whether these AI-generated compounds are both synthesizable and biologically active, demonstrating a workflow for validating machine-learning-generated drug candidates.

papers.title: Computational design and evaluation of tacrine-based carbamate derivatives as acetylcholinesterase inhibitors.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease is marked by a gradual decline in cognitive function accompanied by alterations in cholinergic signaling. Cholinergic function can be improved by targeting acetylcholinesterase (AChE). In this work, an in silico approach was applied to study a series of tacrine-based carbamate derivatives. 3D-QSAR models determined by CoMFA and CoMSIA and validated by cross-validation, external testing and Y-randomization were developed using a dataset of 27 compounds. A complementary 2D-QSAR model provided consistent results to support the proposed structure-activity relationships. The sta
papers.summary: This study uses computational methods (3D-QSAR, 2D-QSAR, and molecular docking) to analyze a series of tacrine-based carbamate derivatives as potential acetylcholinesterase inhibitors for Alzheimer's disease. The models identified key structural features that enhance inhibitory activity, providing a framework for designing improved AChE inhibitors.

papers.title: Molecular Docking and Prediction of ADMET/Drug-Likeness Properties of Potential Bioactive Anti-Rheumatoid Arthritis Compounds Isolated From the Essential Oil of Capparis Spinosa L. Leaves.
papers.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease and one of the most prevalent complex inflammatory disorders. Capparis spinosa L. (C. spinosa) is recognized for its diverse medicinal properties. Traditionally, the plant has been employed to alleviateconditions such as paralysis, gastrointestinal infections, rheumatism, diabetes, anemia, pain, and eye infections. This study aimed to investigate the potential interactions and predicted pharmacological relevance of major compounds identified in the essential oil of C. spinosa leaves using computational approaches.
papers.summary: This study uses molecular docking and ADMET/drug-likeness prediction to evaluate major compounds from Capparis spinosa leaf essential oil as potential anti-rheumatoid arthritis agents. The computational analysis suggests these natural compounds may interact with RA-related targets and possess favorable pharmacokinetic properties, though experimental validation is lacking.

papers.title: Gaps in AI-Driven Pharmacokinetic Property Prediction for Early Drug Development: A Scoping Review.
papers.abstract: Machine learning applications in preclinical drug development have been focused on automated covariate selection in pharmacometric modeling and high-throughput screening processes early in drug discovery. While inherent drug property prediction has made significant improvements in the past decade, fusing early target-based drug discovery methods to preclinical stage pharmacokinetic (PK) property predictions has been limited. This scoping review investigates the current state of PK property prediction of small molecules in drug discovery using machine learning methods and a combination of machi
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: This scoping review surveys how machine learning is currently used to predict pharmacokinetic (PK) properties of small molecules in early drug development, finding that most efforts focus on automated covariate selection and high-throughput screening rather than integrating target-based discovery with PK prediction. The authors highlight a significant gap: fusing early target-based drug discovery methods with preclinical PK property predictions remains limited, despite a decade of improvements in inherent drug property prediction.

papers.title: Design, synthesis, biological evaluation, and in silico studies of novel pyrrolidine based hybrids bearing indole, chromone, and benzoylthiourea pharmacophores as multitarget hCA and AChE inhibitors.
papers.abstract: In this study, novel pyrrolidine-based compounds bearing indole, chromone, and benzoylthiourea pharmacophores were rationally designed, synthesized, and evaluated as dual inhibitors of carbonic anhydrase I/II (hCA I, hCA II) and acetylcholinesterase (AChE). The target compounds were synthesized via imine azomethine ylide 1,3-dipolar cycloaddition and in selected cases, benzoyl isothiocyanate condensation reactions. Their structures were fully characterized using FTIR, NMR, microanalysis, and single-crystal X-ray diffraction (for 1ba). Compound 2ad (hCA I, Ki = 35.56 ± 5.10 nM, hCA II, Ki = 31.
papers.summary: This paper reports the design and synthesis of novel pyrrolidine-based hybrid compounds combining indole, chromone, and benzoylthiourea pharmacophores, aiming to create dual inhibitors of carbonic anhydrase (hCA I/II) and acetylcholinesterase (AChE). The compounds were synthesized via 1,3-dipolar cycloaddition and characterized by spectroscopy and X-ray crystallography, with one compound (2ad) showing nanomolar inhibition of hCA I and II. In silico studies were also performed to rationalize the multitarget activity.

papers.title: Three privileged scaffolds, one pipeline: chalcones, pyrazolines and pyrazoles in drug discovery and fluorescent sensing.
papers.abstract: Chalcones, pyrazolines, and pyrazoles constitute a uniquely powerful discovery pipeline in which each is a privileged scaffold with distinct applications, while also serving as the synthetic precursor to the next. Despite a theoretical chalcone library exceeding 680 000 unique structures accessible from commercial starting materials alone, fewer than 5140 examples have been reported in the literature-representing just 0.8% of this chemical space. Combining this precursor library with the downstream pyrazoline and pyrazole chemical spaces yields a combined landscape conservatively estimated to
papers.summary: This review highlights chalcones, pyrazolines, and pyrazoles as privileged scaffolds that form a sequential synthetic pipeline, where each compound class serves as the precursor to the next. The authors note that despite a theoretical chalcone library exceeding 680,000 structures, only about 0.8% have been reported, revealing a vast unexplored chemical space for drug discovery and fluorescent sensing applications.

papers.title: Evaluating the Incremental Value of Three-Dimensional Conformer Descriptors for Blood-Brain Barrier Permeability Prediction Using the B3DB Benchmark Dataset.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Predicting blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability remains a major challenge in central nervous system (CNS) drug discovery. Three-dimensional (3D) conformer-derived molecular descriptors are often proposed as improvements over conventional two-dimensional (2D) topological representations; however, their incremental predictive value remains unclear. Methods: Here, we systematically evaluated six molecular feature sets comprising curated 2D Mordred descriptors, Morgan/ECFP4 fingerprints, 3D conformer-derived descriptors, and their combinations, using LightGBM regression on
papers.summary: This study systematically tested whether 3D conformer-derived molecular descriptors improve blood-brain barrier permeability prediction over standard 2D descriptors and fingerprints. Using the B3DB benchmark and LightGBM regression, they compared six feature sets including 2D Mordred descriptors, Morgan/ECFP4 fingerprints, 3D conformer descriptors, and combinations. The work clarifies the incremental value of 3D information for CNS drug discovery models.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence in rheumatoid arthritis: current applications and future perspectives.
papers.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a highly prevalent systemic autoimmune disease characterized by a complex and partially understood pathogenesis. The substantial challenges in early identification and marked therapeutic heterogeneity pose a significant burden on affected patients. Despite notable advancements in diagnostic techniques and therapeutic interventions in recent years, optimal patient care remains hindered by several ongoing clinical challenges. To address these limitations, artificial intelligence (AI) has been increasingly integrated into the field of rheumatology. By leveraging its p
papers.summary: This review examines how artificial intelligence is being applied to rheumatoid arthritis, covering current uses in diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment selection. It highlights that AI may help address persistent clinical challenges such as early identification and therapeutic heterogeneity, while also discussing future directions for the field.

papers.title: A comprehensive review of AI innovations for tackling antimicrobial resistance.
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) represents a major global public health concern, rendering available antimicrobials ineffective and leading to infections that are difficult to treat. Artificial intelligence (AI) has been increasingly applied across the AMR continuum, including resistance prediction, rapid diagnostics, new antimicrobial discovery, drug repurposing, antimicrobial surveillance, and clinical decision support. In this review, we aim to highlight recent developments in the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to address antimicrobial resistance (AMR). In addition, we review computatio
papers.summary: This review surveys recent applications of artificial intelligence across the antimicrobial resistance landscape, covering resistance prediction, rapid diagnostics, discovery of new antimicrobials, drug repurposing, surveillance, and clinical decision support. It synthesizes how computational methods are being deployed to address the growing global challenge of drug-resistant infections.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence-driven identification and mechanistic exploration of synergistic anti-aging compounds from Dengzhan Shengmai formulation.
papers.abstract: Aging is a complex biological process involving multiple dysregulated pathways, and synergistic compound combinations offer distinct therapeutic advantages through multi-target and multi-pathway interactions. Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) formulations are inherently synergistic, yet systematically identifying their active anti-aging combinations remains a major challenge. Here, we developed DeepSMCA, a deep learning-based framework integrating molecular descriptors, ADMET parameters, and protein-protein interaction (PPI) network embeddings learned via a variational graph auto-encoder (VGA
papers.summary: The authors developed DeepSMCA, a deep learning framework that combines molecular descriptors, ADMET properties, and protein-protein interaction network embeddings to identify synergistic anti-aging compound combinations from the traditional Chinese medicine formulation Dengzhan Shengmai. The approach aims to systematically uncover multi-target active combinations that are difficult to find through conventional screening.

papers.title: In Silico Identification of Natural-Product Aromatase (CYP19A1) Inhibitors via Integrated Molecular Docking and QSAR Modelling.
papers.abstract: Aromatase (CYP19A1) is the rate-limiting enzyme in estrogen biosynthesis and the principal therapeutic target for estrogen receptor-positive (ER+) breast cancer. Despite the clinical success of third-generation aromatase inhibitors (AIs) such as letrozole and anastrozole, acquired resistance and systemic adverse effects, including musculoskeletal pain, bone density loss, and cardiovascular complications, which necessitate the identification of novel scaffolds. This study employs an integrated computational pipeline combining ligand-based quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) mode
papers.summary: This study uses computational methods—combining molecular docking and QSAR modeling—to screen natural products for their ability to inhibit aromatase (CYP19A1), a key enzyme in estrogen production and a target for ER+ breast cancer therapy. The goal is to identify new chemical scaffolds that could overcome resistance and side effects associated with current drugs like letrozole and anastrozole.

papers.title: De Novo Molecular Design and Bioactivity Prediction of Novel Hexahydroquinolines as Plasmodium falciparum Calcium-Dependent Protein Kinase 4 (CDPK4) Inhibitors.
papers.abstract: Plasmodium falciparum Calcium-Dependent Protein Kinase 4 (PfCDPK4) is a validated target for malaria transmission-blocking interventions, as its inhibition disrupts male gametocyte exflagellation. Hexahydroquinolines (HHQs) have emerged as promising gametocytocidal agents. This study aimed to design novel HHQs as potential PfCDPK4 inhibitors with good binding affinity, favourable pharmacokinetics, and structural stability. A library of 20,000 novel HHQ analogs was generated using genetic algorithm-driven de novo molecular design in AlvaBuilder and systematically filtered through a pipeline com
papers.summary: This study used genetic algorithm-driven de novo molecular design to generate 20,000 novel hexahydroquinoline analogs and filtered them for potential activity against Plasmodium falciparum CDPK4, a validated malaria transmission-blocking target. The pipeline combined bioactivity prediction, pharmacokinetic profiling, and structural stability assessment to identify promising inhibitor candidates.

papers.title: Repurposing MK0873 as a non-covalent hTERT-Targeting compound: a proof of concept study.
papers.abstract: Telomerase is a key regulator of both cellular immortality and aging, making it an attractive target for cancer therapy and age associated pathologies. Its clinical exploitation has been limited by structural complexity and challenges in achieving specificity. Recent structural insights into human telomerase reverse transcriptase (hTERT) have enabled the identification of selective inhibitors. Here, we repurposed MK0873, a PDE4 inhibitor previously evaluated in Phase II clinical trials for rheumatoid arthritis and COPD, as a non covalent telomerase targeting agent. In silico docking and molecu
papers.summary: The study repurposes MK0873, a PDE4 inhibitor previously tested in Phase II trials for inflammatory diseases, as a non-covalent inhibitor of human telomerase reverse transcriptase (hTERT) using in silico docking and molecular dynamics. This proof-of-concept suggests a potential new route to telomerase-targeted therapies for cancer and age-related diseases by leveraging an existing clinical-stage drug.

papers.title: Targeting IDH-driven Oncometabolism in glioblastoma: a computational approach for the identification of potential inhibitors.
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is a malignant brain tumor frequently driven by mutations in isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH1 and IDH2) enzymes, which promote neomorphic synthesis of the oncometabolite 2-hydroxyglutarate (2-HG) and subsequent metabolic dysfunction. Although these mutations are associated with different clinical outcomes, therapeutic intervention remains challenging due to tumor heterogeneity, cellular plasticity, restricted blood-brain barrier permeability, drug efflux mechanisms, and effective DNA repair pathways. Therefore, this study aims to identify selective inhibitors of mutant IDH pro
papers.summary: This study uses computational methods to identify potential selective inhibitors of mutant IDH1 and IDH2 enzymes, which drive glioblastoma through production of the oncometabolite 2-hydroxyglutarate. The work targets a well-known cancer metabolic vulnerability, though the abstract is truncated and the specific compounds or validation results are not described.

papers.title: Elucidating adverse drug reactions and underlying molecular mechanisms of ivermectin through pharmacovigilance and multi-omics analysis.
papers.abstract: The comprehensive safety profile and underlying molecular mechanisms of ivermectin-associated adverse drug reactions (ADRs) remain to be fully elucidated.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study combines pharmacovigilance data with multi-omics analysis to characterize adverse drug reactions associated with ivermectin and explore their underlying molecular mechanisms. It aims to provide a more comprehensive safety profile for ivermectin, a drug widely used for parasitic infections and controversially for COVID-19.

papers.title: Naringenin as a dual-target modulator of RAGE-NF-κB signaling and Aβ fibrillization in Alzheimer's disease: integrated computational and experimental analyses.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a complex neurodegenerative disorder characterized by the accumulation and aggregation of β-amyloid (Aβ) and chronic neuroinflammation mediated by the receptor for advanced glycation end products (RAGE). Current therapeutic candidates targeting RAGE signaling or Aβ aggregation continue to face challenges, including off-target toxicity, poor blood-brain barrier (BBB) penetration, and limited multi-target efficacy.
papers.summary: This study investigates naringenin, a natural flavonoid, as a potential dual-target treatment for Alzheimer's disease. Using computational modeling and experimental assays, the authors show that naringenin can both inhibit RAGE-NF-κB inflammatory signaling and interfere with Aβ fibril formation. The findings suggest a multi-target strategy that may overcome limitations of current single-target AD therapies.

papers.title: Comparative and Subtractive Genomics Analysis of Multidrug-Resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae Strains for Novel Target Identification and Drug Repurposing Strategies.
papers.abstract: The rapid rise of multidrug-resistant (MDR) Klebsiella pneumoniae has created a major global health challenge due to the limited availability of conserved therapeutic targets effective across diverse resistant strains. In this study, an integrative computational target-discovery and drug-repurposing framework was applied to six clinically relevant K. pneumoniae strains. Comparative genomic analysis identified 3012 conserved genes, which were subsequently filtered to nine essential, non-host homologous proteins. Among these, three conserved cytoplasmic proteins (accD, cpxR, and mraZ) were prior
papers.summary: This study used comparative and subtractive genomics to identify conserved drug targets across six multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae strains, narrowing 3012 conserved genes down to nine essential, non-host-homologous proteins. Three cytoplasmic proteins (accD, cpxR, and mraZ) were prioritized as promising targets, and the authors applied drug repurposing strategies to find existing compounds that could inhibit them. The work provides a computational framework for identifying new therapeutic options against antibiotic-resistant infections.

papers.title: Sesamum indicum-derived valdiate as a novel neuroprotective agent targeting PDE10A2 and SIRT1 in Huntington's disease.
papers.abstract: Huntington's disease is prevalent globally, with approximately 4.88 cases per 100,000 people, based on a systematic review and meta-analysis of 33 studies published between 2010 and 2022. Despite its significant prevalence, no proper treatment is available that directly addresses Huntington's disease. The existing treatments focus on symptom management, such as controlling chorea and psychiatric symptoms. The drugs used for this purpose may also cause side effects, including depression and Parkinson's disease.
papers.summary: This study investigates a compound derived from Sesamum indicum (sesame) as a potential neuroprotective agent for Huntington's disease, targeting the proteins PDE10A2 and SIRT1. Using bioinformatics approaches, the authors identify and validate this natural compound as a novel therapeutic candidate that could address the lack of treatments directly targeting the disease. The work highlights a plant-derived molecule as a promising starting point for Huntington's disease drug development.

papers.title: Fighting the invader: strategies against intracellular bacteria.
papers.abstract: Intracellular pathogenic bacteria are often-overlooked agent of chronic, recurrent and difficult-to-treat infections in a context of escalating antimicrobial resistance. By hiding within professional and non-professional phagocytes, adopting dormant or slow-replicative states and rewiring host pathways, these pathogens successfully evade both immune clearance and conventional antibiotic therapy, thus contributing to treatment failure and, potentially, carcinogenesis. Here we synthesise how obligate and facultative intracellular bacteria invade and persist within host cells, and interpret these
papers.summary: This review synthesizes the mechanisms by which obligate and facultative intracellular bacteria invade host cells, persist in dormant or slow-replicating states, and evade both immune clearance and conventional antibiotics. It highlights how these pathogens contribute to chronic, recurrent, and hard-to-treat infections, and potentially to carcinogenesis, in the context of rising antimicrobial resistance. The authors discuss strategies to combat these intracellular invaders.

papers.title: Computational blueprint and stereochemical validation of a small peptide derived from Lacticaseibacillus casei VITCM05 targeting estrogen receptor alpha and human epidermal growth factor receptor 2.
papers.abstract: Breast cancer remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality among women worldwide, necessitating the development of safer and more targeted therapeutic strategies. This study computationally extends our previous experimental investigation of a peptide derived from Lacticaseibacillus casei by evaluating its interactions with two clinically relevant breast cancer targets, estrogen receptor alpha (ERα; PDB ID: 3ERT) and human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2; PDB ID: 1N8Z).
papers.summary: This study computationally models how a small peptide from the probiotic bacterium Lacticaseibacillus casei binds to two breast cancer drug targets, estrogen receptor alpha (ERα) and HER2. Using molecular docking and stereochemical validation, the authors propose that the peptide could interact with both receptors, extending their earlier experimental work. The findings are preliminary and would require wet-lab validation to confirm therapeutic potential.

papers.title: Repositioning antiviral phytoconstituents as broad-spectrum inhibitors of influenza A neuraminidase and human metapneumovirus fusion protein.
papers.abstract: Viral respiratory infections still exist as a major global health concern. Influenza A viruses and human metapneumoviruses are among the main pathogens responsible for infections that can progress to severe acute respiratory forms. Despite the availability of certain therapeutic options, the need for effective treatment remains an issue. The exploration of innovative approaches based on medicinal plants, capable of simultaneously targeting several viruses, represents a promising strategic option for limiting the viral activity of these pathogens. In this work, an integrated computational workf
papers.summary: This study uses an integrated computational workflow to screen antiviral phytoconstituents (plant-derived compounds) as potential dual inhibitors of influenza A neuraminidase and human metapneumovirus fusion protein. The goal is to identify broad-spectrum natural compounds that could target both respiratory viruses simultaneously, offering a promising alternative to existing limited therapeutic options.

papers.title: Molecular Characterization of DENV-1 Isolates From Pakistan Reveals Immunogenic Variability and Antiviral Potential of Phytochemicals Targeting the CprM Region.
papers.abstract: Dengue virus (DENV), a mosquito-borne arbovirus, remains a critical global health concern, causing approximately 390 million infections annually. Dengue fever poses significant challenges to healthcare systems in endemic regions like Pakistan due to the presence of four established serotypes (DENV-1-DENV-4) and the potential emergence of a fifth serotype (DENV-5). The current study aimed to investigate molecular characteristics of DENV-1 isolates from Peshawar, Pakistan, focusing on serotyping, genetic variability in the CprM junction region, and identification of potential antiviral phytochem
papers.summary: This study characterizes DENV-1 isolates from Peshawar, Pakistan, by sequencing the CprM junction region and analyzing genetic variability that may affect immunogenicity. The authors also screen phytochemicals for potential antiviral activity against this region, identifying candidates for further development. The work highlights the importance of local DENV-1 molecular surveillance and plant-derived compounds as possible therapeutics.

papers.title: Computational identification and evaluation of Adenium obesum phytochemicals as potential EGFR inhibitors for targeted therapy against non-small-cell lung cancer.
papers.abstract: Non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains the leading cause of lung cancer-related mortality, largely driven by aberrant activation of the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR). Despite the clinical success of EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs), intrinsic and acquired resistance, coupled with safety concerns, highlight the need for novel, safer inhibitors. Natural products represent an underexplored source of structurally diverse bioactive compounds with favorable biocompatibility. In this study, a comprehensive in silico approach is used to evaluate phytochemicals from Adenium obesum a
papers.summary: This study uses computational docking and simulation to screen phytochemicals from the ornamental plant Adenium obesum as potential inhibitors of EGFR, a key driver of non-small-cell lung cancer. Several compounds showed favorable predicted binding and drug-like properties, suggesting they warrant further experimental testing as alternatives to existing EGFR inhibitors that face resistance issues.
